title: Replication spec for Measuring inequality and social stratification with Lorenz curvature
hypothesis: A continuous family of inequality/stratification indices I_p = ||kappa(L)||_p with stratification-aversion alpha=p-1 measures total Lorenz curvature kappa = L''/(1+L'^2)^{3/2}. Anonymity/scale/population invariance hold for all p. Normalizability, Pigou-Dalton and Lorenz dominance hold iff p=1 (alpha=0) and then only weakly for Pigou-Dalton. For any p>1 they can fail. Empirically I_1 deviates consistently from Gini/Atkinson/Amato-Kakwani/Theil/P90/P10/Wolfson rank orderings on PIP percentile data, less so for consumption-based than income-based countries.
data_sources: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform PIP percentile shares https://github.com/ahippelainen/curvature_inequality CC-BY 4.0
sample: Country Lorenz curves reconstructed from PIP percentile shares, latest yearly dataset available per nation. Analysis dataset = countries with reportable percentile shares. Total N=172 for curvature maximum diagnostic. Split by PIP welfare concept: income-based N=72 and consumption-based N=100. Visualization/reordering demo subsample: income-measured 12 nations [Australia,Brazil,Chile,Colombia,France,Germany,Mexico,Poland,Sweden,Turkey,United Kingdom,United States] and consumption-measured 12 nations [China,Egypt,Ethiopia,India,Indonesia,Cote d'Ivoire,Kenya,Morocco,Nigeria,South Africa,Thailand,Vietnam]. Comparison indices computed on same 12+12 subsamples and on full 72+100 samples. No other filters stated.
period_end: not stated - latest yearly dataset per nation as available in PIP at time of collection
method: 1. Collect PIP percentile share vectors per country, latest year per country. Group by income vs consumption reporting.
2. Visualization sample: fix 12 income countries and 12 consumption countries listed in sample.
3. Full correlation sample: include all countries with data: 72 income-based, 100 consumption-based (total 172 for curvature diagnostic).

4. Reconstruct continuous Lorenz curve L(x) with L(0)=0, L(1)=1, monotone convex, L in C^a(0,1) a>=2. Baseline fit: Bernstein polynomial order M=20 L(x)=sum_{k=0}^M c_k B_{k,M}(x), B_{k,M}=binom(M,k) x^k (1-x)^{M-k} with constraints c0=0,cM=1, c_k<=c_{k+1}, c_{k+2}-2c_{k+1}+c_k>=0, minimize squared residuals. Sample on Gauss-Lobatto grid, derivatives via pseudospectral differentiation matrices. Robustness: refit with M=15 and M=25. Alternative endpoint-derivative schemes: finite-difference derivative and Savitzky-Golay 3rd-order polynomial to first/last 13 points for I_1.

5. Define curvature kappa(L(x))=L''(x)/(1+L'(x)^2)^{3/2} and I_p=(int_0^1 kappa(x)^p dx)^{1/p}=||kappa||_p, 1<=p<=infty, p=infty supremum norm, alpha=p-1 stratification-aversion. Closed form p=1: I_1=L'(1)/sqrt(1+L'(1)^2)-L'(0)/sqrt(1+L'(0)^2)=y_max/mu /sqrt(1+(y_max/mu)^2)-y_min/mu /sqrt(1+(y_min/mu)^2). Operational I_1^delta=L'(1-delta)/sqrt(1+L'(1-delta)^2)-L'(delta)/sqrt(1+L'(delta)^2) approximated from x=0 to 1st percentile and 99th percentile to x=1.

6. Axiomatic/normalizability pathology: kinked sequence F_epsilon(x)=x-x0+sqrt((x-x0)^2+epsilon), L_epsilon=(F_epsilon(x)-F_epsilon(0))/(F_epsilon(1)-F_epsilon(0)) with example x0=3/4. Dominance counterexample: L1(x)=x^3 vs L2(x)=x+0.5*(sqrt((x-0.5)^2+epsilon)-sqrt(0.25+epsilon)) with demo epsilon=10^{-3}, x0=0.5, find p where I_p equal, approx 1.87; monotonicity via Holder: for q>=p ||kappa||_p <= ||kappa||_q. Pigou-Dalton test via bump phi in C^infty_c(a,b), phi>=0, phi(a)=phi'(a)=phi''(a)=phi(b)=phi'(b)=phi''(b)=0, L_epsilon=L+epsilon phi, variation sign condition (kappa^{p-1}/A^3)''+(3 L''L' kappa^{p-1}/A^5)' <0 with A=sqrt(1+L'^2).
7. Alpha sensitivity: compute rankings for alpha in [0.01,10] on 12+12 visualization samples, note swaps. Stable outside window.

8. Comparison indices on same L (Eq. 7 in paper): G=1-2 int L, A_{0.5}=1-(int sqrt(L') )^2, K=(int sqrt(1+L'^2)-sqrt(2))/(2-sqrt(2)), T1=int L' ln L', P90/P10=L'(0.9)/L'(0.1), W=2*(1-2L(0.5)-G)/L'(0.5) with Atkinson epsilon=0.5 baseline. Report ordinal ranks 1-12 per Table 1/2.

9. Full-sample rank correlations: for 72 income and 100 consumption orderings compute Spearman and Kendall matrices among 7 indices [I1,G,A0.5,K,T1,P90/P10,W] displayed as heatmaps Figures 8/9 without numeric values quoted. Robustness of Kendall differences checked for Bernstein orders 15/20/25.
